be carried on the surface of water

<laam>, fathom, and <thum>, three, written as one word: three fathoms

<laam> float with <to>, upward, and the causative <sak>

island and federal territory of Malaysia off the coast of Borneo

<labu>, songbook, with the plural <te>

<la> and <dem> written as one word: compete with others in singing, a song competition
<la>, here the verb take, and the future marker <ding> written as one word: will take, is to take; {tavuan lading} is will take the responsibility

form of <lak>, show, used before <ding>, <nading>, <theih> and nouns: let someone see a thing, or make a quality such as power or kindness known
emphatic particle after a noun or verb that sets one fact beside another: indeed, as for, and yet
the particle <lah.2>, and yet, with <hilo>, is not: placed after a noun or clause to deny it beside another, is not that either; said twice, {A lah hilo, B lah hilo}, it means neither A nor B

{lah ing}, the verb <lah> with the first person ending <ing>, written short with an apostrophe as is done in songs, where the count of words is fixed; the page gives {lah ing e} and {lah'ng e} as the same
a man of Judah, son of Jahath, of the clans of the Zorathites
<lah> and <ding> written as one word: to be shown, something to show
form of <lakkhia> used before <loh>, <ding>, <nading> and nouns: show openly, make known, bring a person out before others
<lahkhiat>, show openly, with the noun suffix {-na}: the act of showing or making something known, a display or presentation of it
grammar term: pointing out, demonstrative, as in <lahkhiatna mintaang>, demonstrative pronoun
an adjective that points out which one is meant and answers the question <koi>, which, as <hih>, <hihte>, <hua>, <huate>, <tua> and <tuate>
grammar term: a pronoun that points at and shows a thing, as <hih>, <hihte>, <hua>, <huate>; <lahkhiatna> is showing

<lah> show with <kholh>, beforehand, and the noun suffix <na>; {lim lahkholhna} is a shadow or picture shown in advance
<lah> show with <kim>, every part, and the noun suffix <na>; {lahkimna lim} is a sketch that shows every detail
<lah>, show, and <kul>, must, written as one word: it is necessary to show a document or proof
town in the western lowland of Judah, listed with Kabbon and Kitlish
town in the western lowland of Judah, listed with Kabbon and Kitlish; another spelling of <Lahmam>
brother of Goliath the Gittite, killed by Elhanan son of Jair
<lah>, show, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of showing or making known, or the thing that shows it; {lim lahna} is the showing of a sign
<lahna>, showing, with the marker <ah> written after a hyphen: in showing a thing; {awsang lahna-ah} is for showing a high tone
<lahna> showing with the plural <te>, the things someone has shown; {lam lahnate} are guideposts
<lah>, show, and <nop>, want, written as one word in a dependent clause: wish to show or make known a thing or a feeling
the person to whom one wants to show something; <lah> show, with <nop> want and <mi> person
what something is meant to show or stand for; <lah> show, with <nop> want and the noun suffix <na>
a wild stinging or thorny plant that overgrows ruins, named together with <thangling>, thistle
<la>, song, and <hoih>, good, written as one word; the pair {thuhoih lahoih}, good words and good songs, stands for wholesome things to hear
<lahoih>, good song, with the plural <te>
a large city in the Punjab province of Pakistan
<lah>, show, with <sa> for a completed action: have shown; before a noun, that which was shown
<lah>, show, with <san>, toward: hold up the fist against someone
<lahsa> shown, with the plural <te>
<lah> show with the plural <te>, making a noun, the things that someone shows; {nalamdang lahte} are the signs shown
<lah>, show, with <tel>, clearly: make something plain or prove it; {lahtel nading} is evidence or proof
<lahtel>, show clearly, with <na> and plural <te>: things set out plainly
<lah>, show, with <theih>, be able; {lahtheih nadingin} means so that one may show

a people of Shan State in Myanmar and of neighbouring countries

written words, a document or anything set down in writing
a written message sent to someone
placed after a verb, before <hi> or <uh>: the state or action goes on, still; {om lai} is there is still, remains
the time when something was so, after <tua> or <hun> and before <in> or <mahin>: {tua lai in} is at that time
the middle of a place, as in {lamka lai-a}, in the middle of the crossroads; compare <laizang>
<lai>, writing, with a capital in {Lai Siangtho}, Holy Scripture, the Bible
the marks that order written text, such as <comma> and <fullstop>; the book gives the English word punctuation for it

terms: as far back as/long ago/already back when
definition: <lai.4>, the time when, and <pekin>, long ago: after a year, a number of years or a clause, already at that time long ago, as far back as; it says that something began or was so that early

terms: may it go on/may it continue
definition: <lai>, still, yet, and <tahen>, may it be: ends a wish or blessing that something go on, placed after a verb, often after <semsem>, more and more, as in {Topa'n hong zang semsem lai tahen}, may the Lord go on using you more and more
<lai>, middle, with the place marker <a>; {lamka lai-a} is in the middle of the crossroads
<lai>, the spot or point, with the place marker <ah>: {hih lai-ah} is here, at this place, and {koi lai-ah} is where, at which place
<lai>, writing, with <aw>, voice: a letter that stands for a vowel, also called <awsuaksak>
literally two vowel letters, one sound: two vowels written together and spoken as a single sound, as {-ia} and {-ua}
<lai>, letter, with <ip>, bag: the cover in which a letter is sent, on which the address is written; given by the book as a noun joined to a noun
the address of the writer or of the receiver, written at the top of a letter; the sample letter has the school and the town there
a stringed instrument, named beside harp and <laiza>; probably the English word lyre

terms: at the time of/in the days of/during
definition: {laia}, written in lower case, is <lai>, time, with the linking <a>: of or at the time named before it, as {tua hun laia}, of that time, and {nidang laia}, of former days; not the instrument
<lai> place with the place marker <ah>, in {tua laiah}, there; more often written <lai-ah>
<lai>, writing, and <at>, write, written as one word: the act of writing, or what someone has written; {laiat pa} is the writer

terms: make a will/draw up a document
definition: <lai>, writing, with <bawl>, make; {a laibawl pa} is the man who made the will
<laibawl>, draw up a document, with the ending <na>: an agreement set down in writing; {kilemna laibawlna} is a peace agreement and {thukimna laibawlna} a memorandum of understanding
<lai>, writing or letter, and <bek>, only, written as one word
a book or scroll that holds writing
a written account or register of people and events
book, capitalised as part of the title of a named book
<laibu>, book, with <pi>, big, written as one word: a large book, also the main book in which records are kept
<laibu>, book, with <saal>, storehouse, written as one word: a library; also used as the title of a collection of writings
plural of <laibu>: books or scrolls
a sheet or surface to write on; a scroll when it is rolled up
an official paper that shows who a person is or what is granted, as {UN laidal}, the refugee document of the UNHCR, and {appointment laidal}; not a blank sheet to write on

<laidal>, an official document, and <tawi>, hold: a person who holds such a document, most often {UN laidal tawi} or {UNHCR laidal tawi}, a refugee registered with the UNHCR and holding its card; it stands after the name of the document, in lists of detained persons after the person's name, and takes <te> for the plural
<laidal> and <neu> written as one word: a small sheet of paper or card with something written on it
<laidal>, sheet of writing, with the ending {-no}, small: a small written sheet, such as a short note or letter, a receipt slip or a religious tract
<laidal>, sheet, with <pi>, big: a full sheet of paper; in the news the paper letter that a refugee holds instead of a card
plural of <laidal>; {savun laidalte} are sheets of skin, parchments
<lai>, still, and <dep>, indeed, written as one word after the verb and before <hi> or {uh hi}: still doing so, and that is notable
<lai>, here still, and <diam> written as one word at the end of a question: will it still be so, I wonder whether it will yet
<lai>, here still, and <ding>, the marker of what is to come, written as one word after a verb: will still, is yet to, will go on; with <maw> or <hiam> it asks whether something is to go on
<laiding>, will still, and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word after a verb or a describing word
strike or knock about with force; <gawp> marks violent or thorough action
<lai> writing and <gelh> write as one word; {laigelh nading} is something to write with
the verb used as a noun: the act of writing, or what someone has written, as in {ka laigelh}, my writing; the same as <laigelhna>
<lai>, writing, and <gelhkhiat>, write out, written as one word: what someone writes and puts out, as a post on social media
the act of writing or the thing written
the tool for writing carried by a scribe
<laigelhna>, a writing, with the plural <te>: written works, as the writings of the prophets
<laigelh>, write, with <pa> for a man: the man who wrote a text; a writer also uses it of himself, the present writer
<lai> and <gelhsak> written as one word: have a letter written for oneself by someone else, here by an office
<laigelh>, write, and <siam>, skilled, written as one word: a person skilled at writing, an author
<laigelh>, writer, with the plural <te>: people whose work is writing, such as secretaries and scribes
<laigelh> with the plural <te>: things that someone has written, such as letters, dispatches and the writings of the prophets
<laigelh>, writing, and <zia>, way, written as one word: how a person writes, the conventions followed in writing
the rules of how a language is written, its orthography
the innermost and most important part of something; <thu laigil> is the heart of a matter
<laigil>, core, with the plural <te>: the central and most important parts of a matter; {Pasian thu laigilte} is the heart of the word of God
<lai>, writing, with <gual>, row: a line of written text, a sentence
<laigual>, sentence, with <picing>, full-grown: a sentence that is complete in itself; two of them may be joined by <ngaklang>, the semicolon
<laigual>, sentence, with the ending {-a}: {laiguala zatna} is the use of a word in sentences
<laigual>, sentence, with the marker <in> of the doer
plural of <laigual>: the lines or sentences of a piece of writing
the cord that joins a child to its mother before birth; {laigui zoppihte}, those joined by the same cord, are children of the same mother

plural of <laiguizom>: brothers and sisters born of the same mother
take the place or office of another, or put one thing in place of another; {galvil laih} is change the guard
<lai>, writing or study, and <hanciam>, strive, written as one word: make an effort in one's studies
in the middle between high and low or large and small; {mi laihawl} is the middle class and {sumlut laihawl gam} a middle-income country

plural of <laihawm>: papers and magazines that are given out regularly

<laihding> and <bek>, only, written as one word: for nothing more than changing it
<lai>, still, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word after a verb or describing word: it is still so, it can still be done

the same pair used of official papers: the documents that allow a person to stay or that an office issues, after <phalna>, permit, or the name of the office
<laikung>, pen, with the subject marker <in> written as one word

the marks that divide and mark off sentences and phrases in writing, punctuation; the lesson lists twelve of them, from <husanna>, comma, to <umtuam>, bracket; also written <lai lepna>

village near Tedim in Chin State; written in brackets after a personal name it tells the home village
cave and old settlement where one group of the people lived before it spread to the Falam, Khalkha, Matupi and Thantlang areas
the middle or inmost part of a thing or of a person, the heart or mind; {ka lailung ah} is in my heart
<lai>, writing, with <mai>, face: one side of a leaf of a book
<lai>, writing, with <mal>, a single item: a written letter or word, or what is written

<laimal>, letter, with <gol>, big: the capital letter with which a sentence begins
<laimal> written letter, with the marker <in> showing means
<laimal>, letter, with {-pi}, big: a capital letter
<laimalpi>, capital letter, with the plural <te>
<laimal>, written letter, with the plural <te>
<lai>, still, and <mawk>, a word of surprise or emphasis, written as one word after a verb: still, even now, and more than one would expect
the Lai people of the Hakha and Falam areas of Chin State, one of the names used among the Chin peoples beside Zomi and Mizo
a place or spot, also a place in a text or talk; {hih laimun ah} is at this place, at this point

a letter that cannot sound by itself and is joined to a vowel to make a word; the book counts B C D F G H J K L M N P Q R S T V W X Y Z and Ng, Kh, Ph, Th, and says F J Q R X Y are little used in Zolai
<la>, take, and <in> written as one word: taking, or as a request with <hong>, come and take
<lai>, still, with the noun-forming ending <na>, placed after a verb, the being still so, as in {a om laina}, those still remaining, {a nuntak laina}, their living on
feel pain within for someone; {nang’ lainat nading} is something for you to be troubled about
<lainat>, feel compassion, with the noun suffix <na>: tender feeling or concern for someone

the soft inner part of a stem or trunk, and so the core or essential part of a matter
written letters or a written text; {laipai khat zong} with a negative is not even a single letter, of one who cannot read or of something done without any writing
<lai>, writing, with <pau>, speech: the written form of a language, in which words such as {kei in} are written out, as opposed to <kampau>, the spoken form
in {khanglui laipek panin}, from the days of old; the exact sense of {laipek} alone is not clear from the verse
<lai>, time, and <pekin>, long ago, written as one word after a describing word: back in the time when it was so
<lai>, a letter or piece of writing, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: the letter, this writing, as the thing spoken about
a written paper handed in or laid before someone, such as a letter of support or the papers of a case; used by one writer
a tall water plant that grows in marshes; {laiphai kungte} are papyrus plants
<lai> and <phi> written as one word: sit a school examination; {tan 10 laiphi} is to sit the tenth standard examination

terms: still for now/for the time being
definition: <lai>, still, and <phot>, for the time being, written as one word after a verb: the action goes on for now
<lai>, time or midst, with the intensifier <pi>, usually followed by <mahin>: at the very time when, right in the midst of; {sunkim laipi} is high noon or broad daylight

<lai>, writing, with <pi>, great: a formal paper given or sent, named by the word before it, as <pahtawina laipi>, a certificate of honour, {ngetna laipi}, an application, {sapna laipi}, an invitation; not the conjunction {laipi}, while still
the religion founded by Pau Cin Hau and the script he made, {Laipian Lai}; also said of its followers and their church
<lai>, letters, with <pil>, wise: learned from books, doing well at school; also a person who is so, as in {laipil khat}
<lai>, letters, and <pilna>, knowledge, written as one word: learning gained from books and school
<lai>, letter, and <puak>, send or deliver, written as one word: a letter that is sent or brought to someone; also the act of delivering it
in {pumpeng laisah}, the reed of which boats are made in Isaiah 18; with a capital, <Laisah> is a place name
town in Benjamin near Gallim and Anathoth, named in the advance of the Assyrian army toward Jerusalem
<lai>, still, with the particle <sam>, indeed, written as one word after a verb: still does so, to be sure; it grants a point, often before a contrast
in {puan laisan}, a traditional woven cloth of the <Zomi>, worn at celebrations and put on a person to honour him
name of the city in the far north that the tribe of Dan captured and renamed Dan, and of the father of Paltiel from Gallim
placed after a clause: for as long as, or to the extent that, it is so; {ahih theih laisiah} is as far as possible
<lai>, writing or study, with <siam>, skilled: learned, well educated or good at school work; also a noun, an educated person
<laisiam>, good at study, with the linking <in>: being good at study, and
<laisiam>, educated, with the noun suffix <na>: being educated, skill in study
<lai>, writing, and <siangtho>, holy, written as one word: the Bible
<lai>, writing, with <sim>, read: read a text; {laisim ngei lo} is never having studied
